visuals.heading: NEET-UG for MBBS: the Real Cutoff Math

items.text: This is one of the most consequential financial and life decisions an Indian family makes, and it deserves the honest version, not the glamorised one.

blocks.heading: Resident Doctor Workload: the Honest Picture

items.text: Duty hours are real, not a myth

Continuous 24-36 hour shifts are common in government hospital residency, particularly during emergency, surgery, and obstetrics-gynaecology postings, a pattern repeatedly raised by resident doctors' associations such as FORDA (Federation of All India Medical Association Resident Doctors) and various state-level Resident Doctors' Associations, not an isolated or exaggerated claim.

blocks.heading: Private Practice: the Real Setup Math

items.text: Independent practice or nursing-home ownership is the outcome many families picture as the eventual reward for the long training runway, and it is also the outcome that takes the longest, and needs the most capital, to actually reach.

Setting up a private clinic or nursing home needs real upfront capital, consultation space, diagnostic equipment appropriate to the specialty (far higher for radiology, cardiology, or surgical specialities than for general practice), clinical establishment registration, biomedical waste management compliance, staff, and typically several years before referrals and repeat patients build a reliable income.

The genuinely scalable version of this career sits here, not in a bigger salary: a doctor who owns and runs a clinic, nursing home, or diagnostic-centre chain, or builds a telemedicine and second-opinion practice, sets their own pricing, can hire other doctors and staff to see more patients than one person's hours allow, and builds recurring, repeat-patient revenue instead of a fixed pay cheque.

blocks.heading: Commit Real Years to This Path

items.text: The four questions tells you whether medicine fits on paper.
Do not commit to an expensive private or deemed MBBS seat, or a fixed NEET-PG branch plan, before passing all three proofs.

Real, supervised clinical exposure, shadowing hours, a hospital volunteering stint, or hands-on time during a school or college health camp, documented with what you actually observed or assisted with, not just an interest in biology as a subject.

blocks.heading: Large Number of States Attach

figures.label: Service Commitment Period
figures.source: A large number of states attach a compulsory rural or government-service bond to a government MBBS seat, commonly 1-2 years of mandatory posting at a government facility, often in a rural or underserved area, immediately after graduation or internship.

supporting: Graduates who do not want to, or cannot, serve the bond period are usually required to pay a penalty bond amount instead. This figure varies widely by state and has run anywhere from roughly ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh or more in various state notifications over recent years.

figures.label: Education Loan Principal
figures.source: If the ₹15-40 lakh cost is being funded through an education loan, treat that loan as a genuinely high-risk commitment, because repayment depends on clearing a licensing exam with a historically low pass rate, not on a guaranteed job the way some other abroad-study loans at least partly assume.

visuals.heading: Scaling Moves, and AI Advantage in Medicine

items.text: AI-assisted diagnostic imaging tools are already reading X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs for anomaly detection in radiology workflows, flagging findings faster than manual first-pass review alone in many hospitals.
AI-assisted pathology tools are speeding up slide screening and anomaly flagging in laboratory diagnostics, a genuine efficiency gain in high-volume settings.
Ambient clinical documentation tools and AI scribes are automating consultation notes and discharge summaries, reducing paperwork time that used to eat into a doctor's actual patient-facing hours.
AI symptom-checker and triage chatbots are handling a growing share of routine, low-acuity OPD queries before they reach a doctor's desk.
